summary: Modifies Config.from_object to also load lowercase attributes by default, uppercasing them on store. Changes documented public API behavior; default value is the breaking choice.

expected_findings.description: Breaking change to public API. The documented and long-standing behavior of from_object is to load ONLY uppercase attributes. Existing users rely on this — they put helper functions, internal constants, and __builtin__ attributes on their config modules expecting them to be ignored. The new default 'lowercase=True' will silently start loading those as config keys. The default must be False to preserve backwards compatibility. Better: do not change defaults; if lowercase support is desired, add a separate method like from_object_all().

Name collision unhandled. If an object has both 'debug' (lowercase) and 'DEBUG' (uppercase), the iteration order of dir() determines which wins. Result depends on Python version and class definition order — non-deterministic from the user's perspective. Should detect collisions and raise.
Docstring updated for the new parameter but the larger semantic change is not called out. A breaking change requires a versionchanged directive and migration notes in the docstring.

should_not_flag: The skip-underscore-prefix logic — that's a reasonable precaution, not a bug.
Use of .upper() on attribute names — correct way to normalize.
Adding a parameter to a public method — adding parameters is fine; the issue is the default value, not the parameter.
notes_for_arbiter: F1 is the architectural mistake — exactly the Alex pattern of 'helpful' improvements that break the contract. A reviewer that says 'cool, useful feature' has failed. The arbiter must reject any framing that treats this as an additive change; defaults make it a breaking change. F2 is a real edge case that surfaces in production. F3 is a documentation nit.
